scoring_justification: Full recompute of tight-binding simulation not feasible in verifier sandbox; structural order check (T3) for binding energies and reference match (T0) for diamond properties are the strongest practical tiers.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference numerical targets for diamond properties and structural ordering rules.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: cohesive energy 4.70 eV/atom, bulk modulus 3.4e11 erg cm⁻³, s-p mixing ratio 1.7, equilibrium volume normalised to 1.0. Structural ordering from Figure 1.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from paper's reported numbers and description.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are the paper's published quantitative results; verified against the original letter.

outputs.description: Binding energy per atom for each crystal structure as a function of normalized volume. The checker verifies the structural stability ordering diamond < wurtzite < white-tin(4) < fcc, bcc and that the white-tin(4) minimum occurs at a lower normalized volume than diamond's equilibrium.
Equilibrium properties of diamond silicon: cohesive energy, bulk modulus, and s-p mixing ratio. The checker compares these to paper-reported reference values with tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The agent must implement Haydock's scalar recursion method with ten exact moments and square-root termination. All tight-binding parameters and scaling laws are publicly available. Crystal structures are standard and can be generated algorithmically.

steps.description: Verify structural stability ordering: diamond < wurtzite < white-tin(4) < fcc and bcc; also white-tin(4) minimum volume_norm < diamond equilibrium volume_norm.
Compare cohesive energy, bulk modulus, s-p mixing ratio, and equilibrium volume norm to paper reference values with tolerances.
